audit.title: DataLink (Pull Delivery)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening — "DataLink pull-based feeds provide access to specialized data from Data Providers through offchain retrieval with onchain verification capabilities." Self-contained and liftable. Section leads ("How It Works", "Getting Started") are also clean.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; clear H2/H3 hierarchy, 0 level skips, numbered steps and bullets. Only gap: no comparison table (e.g., REST vs WebSocket) where one would aid extraction.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 7 numerals, 0 with units, no latency/frequency/network counts, no version strings. "Real-time", "on-demand", "battle-tested" are qualitative-only.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 7 internal links, 0 external/primary. No link to the Data Streams verifier spec or any canonical standard despite repeated "cryptographically signed/verify" claims.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The lead sentence and the "Pull-based delivery" bullet are quotable; "DataLink" itself lacks a crisp standalone gloss distinguishing it from Data Streams.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, 0 og/twitter tags. No freshness or E-E-A-T signal for engines to trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. Acceptable for a hub page, but even a minimal REST fetch snippet would raise agent-runnability and retrieval for "how do I fetch a DataLink report."

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what is", "how it works", "getting started". No troubleshooting/FAQ, no symptom-phrased entries.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; unambiguous, consistent product naming (DataLink, Data Streams, DONs). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured overview/navigation hub for DataLink Pull Delivery — it opens with a serviceable one-sentence definition and cleanly routes to Architecture, Tutorials, and Reference. Its biggest GEO strength is scannability (8 headings, 0 level skips, tight sections). Its biggest weakness is the total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates) combined with thin specifics (268 words, 0 units, 0 version strings, 0 external citations). As a hub page it does its navigation job, but it gives engines little liftable substance and no freshness/authority signals — verdict: functional but under-optimized for direct citation.

recommendations.title: Emit TechArticle JSON-LD + canonical + dateModified
recommendations.change: Add a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `about: "DataLink Pull Delivery"`, canonical URL `https://docs.chain.link/datalink/pull-delivery/overview`, and a visible/structured `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust, directly improving citation eligibility.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to Key Characteristics
recommendations.issue: "Pull-based delivery: Fetch data on-demand via REST API or real-time via WebSocket" — no numbers.
recommendations.change: Add quantified facts: supported network count, report update frequency/latency, verifier-contract chains, SDK languages (Go/Rust) with versions. Even "verification on N EVM chains" beats zero.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for generative visibility; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a crisp DataLink-vs-Data-Streams distinction
recommendations.issue: The page repeatedly ties DataLink to Data Streams ("same underlying infrastructure") but never states what makes DataLink distinct in one liftable sentence.
recommendations.change: Add one sentence: "DataLink differs from Data Streams by sourcing specialized datasets from individual Data Providers rather than aggregated market feeds, while reusing the same APIs, SDKs, and verifier contracts."
recommendations.why: Defends against parametric priors that would collapse DataLink into the more common Data Streams idiom.

recommendations.title: Add a REST vs WebSocket vs Onchain comparison table
recommendations.issue: Three bullets give options but no decision factors — "REST API: Fetch reports on-demand for periodic updates".
recommendations.change: Convert to a 3-row table: Method | Use when | Latency | Trade-off. Let engines extract *reasons*.
recommendations.why: Comparison tables let engines build justified answers to "should I use REST or WebSocket for DataLink."

recommendations.title: Add external/primary citations
recommendations.where: "Onchain verification" bullet and "How It Works" step 2
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; verification claims are unattributed.
recommendations.change: Link "verify report integrity using verifier contracts" to the canonical verifier-contract reference/spec page; link "cryptographically signed reports" to the Data Streams verification spec.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate for the claims they support.

recommendations.title: Add a short symptom/FAQ block
recommendations.issue: No troubleshooting or "how do I…" entries; devs query by symptom.
recommendations.change: Add 2–3 Q-phrased headings, e.g. "How do I fetch a DataLink report via REST?", "Which networks support onchain verification?", each answering in the first sentence with a link.
recommendations.why: Symptom/question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

antiPatterns: Mild marketing qualifiers — "battle-tested", "familiar developer experience", "proven infrastructure" — replace or quantify; they carry no extractable fact.
No dated/freshness signal (stale-risk), per measured "dateModified absent".
No hard cross-reference errors, no keyword stuffing, no ambiguous pronouns — prose is clean.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and og/twitter tags are almost certainly template/site-level fixes — apply once across `docs.chain.link` rather than per page.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; ensure this overview and its child pages are indexed there.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified; here it "could not be captured," so absence is inferred from the served HTML measurement, not head inspection.
